strategy.summary: Reproduce the rolling skew/kurt accuracy bug (degenerate/all-equal data returning incorrect finite values vs NaN) on the buggy pandas revision 027ea1edde4e, and ensure the project regression test fails there and passes on the fixed revision 965ceca9fd796940050d6fc817707bba1c4f9bff (plus associated fixes). The transition is driven by whether nanops/nan-skew/kurt and rolling window skew/kurt treat floating-point degeneracy/tolerance consistently (returning NaN rather than 0 or -3, and not producing NaNs only at some indices).

pinned_because: numpy==1.24.3 is explicitly documented as numerically relevant in issue#53639
pandas build revision is explicitly pinned to 965ceca9fd796940050d6fc817707bba1c4f9bff in the provided context (used as the fixed/transition target); buggy revision is 027ea1edde4e per instance
environment.build_commands_note: If you need to install pandas from source for the exact commits, use editable install from the checked-out repo at the target commit; the context also states Cython is needed for building pandas extensions.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (027ea1edde4e), running the above pytest -k selection should FAIL because pandas rolling skew/kurt returns incorrect values for the specified all-float pattern (specifically it must not match the expected Series where the last windows are NaN). After switching to the fixed pandas revision (965ceca9fd796940050d6fc817707bba1c4f9bff as provided), the same test should PASS because rolling skew/kurt yields the expected NaN propagation for the degenerate/constant window cases.
strategy.numerical_probe: The test asserts exact Series equality (including NaN positions) for rolling skew and rolling kurt on a constructed Series with degenerate values; no additional numeric inspection is required beyond the test’s Series equality assertions.

input_output_examples.input: Rolling skew/kurt on the crafted Series used by test_rolling_skew_kurt_floating_artifacts (filename: pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py).
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Mismatch vs expected Series: buggy revision produces finite values at indices where expected requires NaN (context example shows prior wrong output containing `nan` among other finite values, e.g. `22.231175098311923 nan 22.23117509831192`, but the graded test specifically checks rolling skew/kurt edge NaN placement).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Matches the expected Series in the test: skew expected to be `Series([np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, 1.9619045191072484, 2.0, np.nan, np.nan])` and kurt expected to be `Series([np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, 3.8636048803878786, 4.0, np.nan, np.nan])` for the assertions in the diff provided.

risks: You may need to build pandas from source (installing Cython first) to ensure the Cythonized rolling window aggregations are used; otherwise you could end up running a different code path and not hit the bug.

The provided context pins only numpy==1.24.3; pandas/pytest/scipy/Cython versions are not pinned, so if your local environment uses different versions, numerical/tolerance behavior could differ and affect whether the test transitions.

This strategy assumes the fixed behavior corresponds to the pandas revision 965ceca9fd796940050d6fc817707bba1c4f9bff; if additional dependent commits are required, the test may still fail even on that revision.

If the bug is architecture-dependent (e.g., different floating point semantics), the failing/passing behavior may not reproduce identically on all platforms; the context does not specify an architecture or sanitizer.

oracle.reference_source: Project’s own regression test expectations in pandas/tests/window/test_rolling.py (assert_series_equal against a hard-coded expected Series containing NaNs and specific finite values).
oracle.why: The selected test performs assert_series_equal to compare the entire Series (including NaN placement), so correctness is judged exactly by the test, not by a tolerance-based external reference.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion in test_rolling_skew_kurt_floating_artifacts should fail because pandas rolling skew/kurt on the constructed degenerate Series does not produce the expected NaN pattern at the later indices (i.e., buggy revision returns incorrect finite values where expected is NaN).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After checking out pandas at commit/build revision 965ceca9fd796940050d6fc817707bba1c4f9bff, the same assert_series_equal should succeed: rolling skew and rolling kurt match the expected NaN-at-late-indices Series values exactly.
